title: Carrots, fresh, cooked, no added fat

content.title: About
content.content: Carrots are a root vegetable rich in beta‑carotene, which the body converts to vitamin A. When boiled without added fat they retain most nutrients, stay sweet and tender, and work well as a side dish or in soups and stews.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Carrots were first domesticated in Central Asia over 5,000 years ago.
The orange color became common in the 17th century after Dutch breeders selected for it.
Raw carrot sticks are often used as a natural “toothpick” for cleaning teeth.
Carrots come in many colors: purple, yellow, white and red as well as orange.
In Japan carrots are frequently cut into thin match‑stick strips (julienne).

items.title: Rich source of beta‑carotene
items.content: Beta‑carotene is converted to vitamin A, supporting vision, immunity and skin health.

items.title: Supports cardiovascular health
items.content: Potassium and antioxidants help regulate blood pressure and reduce oxidative stress.

items.title: Provides dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber aids digestion, promotes satiety and supports a healthy gut microbiome.

items.title: Low in calories
items.content: A 100‑g serving of boiled carrots contains about 35 kcal, making it a weight‑friendly option.

items.title: Contains vitamins K and C
items.content: Vitamin K is important for blood clotting, while vitamin C boosts immunity and iron absorption.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: A small number of people may experience an allergic reaction to carrots, such as itching or swelling.

items.title: Excessive beta‑carotene intake
items.content: Very large amounts of carrots can cause carotenemia – a harmless yellowish skin tint that fades after intake is reduced.

items.title: Pesticide residues
items.content: When buying non‑organic carrots, rinse them thoroughly to remove possible chemical residues.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Boiled carrots without added fat can be served as a side dish, added to vegetable stews, soups, salads or pureed. They are also easy to dice or cut into sticks for quick preparation.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store fresh carrots in the refrigerator’s vegetable drawer, preferably in a perforated bag. Keep boiled carrots in an airtight container for 3–4 days.
